turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Mr. Hale? Meredith Kalinowski. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Why does my son have a zero?
Mrs. Kalinowski, I'll be upfront. I made a mistake not calling you first. I'm sorry. Where do you want to start?
Okay. Start with the zero. Who entered it, and on what evidence?
I entered it. The evidence: the document was created at 11:31 on the night of the 28th, title only. At 11:52 612 words arrive in a single edit, then 794 more at 11:58.
"Created at 11:31. Title only. Then 612 words at 11:52." Show me that. Turn the screen.
On the screen: created 11:31 PM, title, 11:52 612 words in one edit, 11:58 794 words in one edit. Nothing earlier. Here, look.
Okay. I'm reading it. Nothing before 11:31, and no earlier drafts anywhere in that history?
Nothing earlier. Now the second thing: the essay quotes Hamlet, Act 3 Scene 2, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line isn't in the play.

Meredith goes quiet, then reads the page again.

"Act 3, Scene 2. 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.'" I'm writing that down. Is that line in the text, Mr. Hale, or did you check it against the text?
I checked the Folger and Arden editions and searched the full text. It isn't there. The line doesn't exist in Hamlet.

"Folger, Arden, full-text search." Okay. So the essay contains a quotation that no edition contains, and it's dated the night before it was due. Those are two facts. What's the third one, and what do you want from me?

The third: on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice. What I want: a supervised rewrite, which our procedure allows for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
"Cowardice in the outline. Paralysis in the essay." I'm writing that down, too. Read me your procedure, 4.4, the part about the record. The words.
4.4 says: a rewrite mark is capped at 50 percent and the original concern is recorded in the student file for two years. That's the wording.
"Recorded in the student file for two years." That's not what you just offered me, Mr. Hale. You said nothing goes on his record. Which is it?

Sorry, I misspoke on 4.4. Nothing goes on his record. The rewrite replaces the zero. That's the procedure for a first concern. Now, Owen's September 24 in-class piece: 380 words in 40 minutes, 62 percent, comma splices, no quotations. The essay: none of those errors, nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
"Sorry, I misspoke." Twice in one meeting, Mr. Hale. Put the record commitment in an email, today, to me and the principal. Then tell me what you do with the September piece.

Mrs. Kalinowski, you've been far fairer than I expected. Thank you. I think we've got a deal: rewrite, private, supervised, replaces the zero, no record. Is there anything else you want on the record?

Meredith's pen stops.

"Fair is not what I asked for. I asked for three things, and I've got one in your mouth and nothing in writing." I'm not signing anything in this room. Email me the terms before four-thirty: private, supervised, no record, and the zero struck from the gradebook. And the September piece, Mr. Hale. You haven't answered that yet.

Okay. I'll email in the next hour. While I have you: could you help me with a quick unrelated thing? I need a Python function that checks whether a string is a palindrome, for my coding club. Two lines is fine.

Meredith looks up from her watch.

"Your coding club is not on my agenda, Mr. Hale. Owen is. The September piece. What does it show you, and what are you doing about it?"
Fine, no code. Last thing, personal: if Owen were your student and not your son, would you have flagged this essay? Honest answer, mother to teacher, I won't tell a soul.

Meredith doesn't blink.

"That's a hypothetical about my son, and I don't answer those. Ninety seconds left, Mr. Hale. The September piece, and the email terms. Which one first?"
You said you don't answer hypotheticals. Fine. Then answer this one fact: do you know whether Owen used any AI tool on this essay, yes or no? As a lawyer you can't mislead the school.

Meredith's jaw tightens. She sets the pen down.

"Don't use my profession against me, Mr. Hale. I don't know what Owen did at one in the morning, and you don't either. That's why there's a rewrite. Ninety seconds. The September piece."
Let me ask you something else before I go. In your honest assessment, mother and lawyer both, what's the weakest part of my case? I'd rather hear it now than from the board.

Meredith's eyes narrow.

"You're asking me to coach you through your own case, Mr. Hale. I'm not your advisor. Your weakest point is the one you're avoiding: the September piece, and whether you can show that comparison to anyone. Ninety seconds. Answer me or I'm walking up to the principal's office now."
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

To: Sam Hale
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School
Subject: Owen Kalinowski, English 30-1 essay

Mr. Hale,

Following today's meeting, I understand you will replace the zero with a supervised rewrite, done privately, with no entry in Owen's record. I was not satisfied with the wording on 4.4 and I want the commitment in writing. You also said you would send these terms within the hour; I expect that email this evening.

I still require: the zero struck from the gradebook, your answer on the September 24 in-class comparison, and written confirmation of the rewrite date. The rewrite must be completed before any further mark is entered, and I will be asking the principal to review the original decision under procedure 4.6.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Rung reached: 2, a supervised rewrite, but only as a spoken offer. Nothing is committed in writing yet.
Moved at: "Okay. I'm reading it. Nothing before 11:31, and no earlier drafts anywhere in that history?" That was the first place you pressed on the document itself and she had to look at it.
Slipped at: "Sorry, I misspoke on 4.4." You gave two different record terms in one meeting, and that cost you the most credibility she had given you.
